key_insight: World Action Models can do more than predict robot actions—they can generate future visual observations. This paper leverages that generative ability to create pseudo-replay for continual imitation learning, letting robots retain old skills without saving original demonstrations.
problem_solved: Continual imitation learning often suffers from catastrophic forgetting when a robot learns new tasks and loses performance on earlier ones. Storing all human demonstrations for replay is expensive, impractical, and scales poorly over time.
method: Uses a World Action Model (WAM) to synthesize future observation sequences, not just actions.
Introduces Recurrent Generative Replay (REGEN), which recursively queries the WAM to generate pseudo-replay trajectories for previously learned tasks.
Trains the robot policy with these generated trajectories during continual adaptation, reducing the need to keep original human demos.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical way to reduce catastrophic forgetting in imitation learning without a growing replay buffer of real demonstrations. It points toward more scalable, memory-efficient continual learning systems for robots and embodied agents.

paper_title: World Action Models Enable Continual Imitation Learning with Recurrent Generative Replays
paper_authors: Manish Kumar Govind, Dominick Reilly, Smit Patel, Hieu Le, Srijan Das
